text_post: I am the father of two sons; Josiah (4yr) and Elijah (2yr), and husband to Jamie. I "woke up" when I started witnessing the differences of how women are treated differently then men. Of how feminism does not care about nor even want to hear about the concerns of men. I come to this site to be help and to find help for those people in my life that are facing these problems. I can currently only offer fear mongering and self preservation... to their own detriment. My sister is a "second wife" to a man with children that they both take care of. She recently got her degree and is now gainfully employed. The "other mother" is a 'recovered' drug addict. I constructed an entirely hypothetical situation that is close enough to reality to cause my sister to take note. "What if she files for custody?" "What stops her from filing for child support?" "Do you think they won't come after your income as well?" That was enough to wake her up as well. But there was not any decisive path to go from there beyond "hoping for the best" as her disaster plan. I have always wanted to be a protector, supporter and provider for my family. I currently do all of these things, but I feel entirely taken advantage of. While examining my own situation, in my own marriage. I feel oppressed. And I have came to the conclusion that to preserve the most options, being in my son's lives, that I am forced to wear this yoke of slavery. All other options are to my own detriment.

text_post: Welcome to the AVFM forums kitty. You'll find that a lot of women start thinking about issues that affect men when they are in the position of being a second wife or a grandmother who has lost access to her son's children. One of the most short sighted aspects of today's family court system is that many children not only lose out on having a father in their lives but they miss out on having cousins, uncles, aunts and grandparents as well. Their paternal family (a huge part of every child's identity) remains a mystery to them. My mother has been a great mentor to my daughter and it would have been a shame if she hadn't had that influence in her life.
